chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Abu Dhamrah, from Ibn Ajlan, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Ride and shoot archery, and for you to shoot is more beloved to me than for you to ride."
Then he said, "Every matter of the believer is vain/trivial except in three: training his horse, shooting with his bow, and playing with his wife, for these are true/right."
Indeed, Allah will admit through a single arrow three people to Paradise: the one who works the wood of it, the one who strengthens it, and the one who shoots it in the cause of Allah.

key_terms.الْمُقَوِّيَ بِهِ: The one who strengthens it (arrow fletcher/straightener)
key_terms.عَامِلَ الْخَشَبِ: The worker of the wood (arrow maker)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things in which a believer's actions are considered truly significant according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) distinguishes between trivial pursuits and three 'true' activities: horse training, archery, and spousal intimacy, framing them as acts of worship that carry spiritual reward. The narration specifically highlights the communal merit of archery, noting that the craftsman, the preparer, and the archer all share in the reward of a single arrow, a concept deeply valued in Shia jurisprudence for understanding shared virtue in jihad. This teaching underscores the balance between physical preparation for battle and domestic life, both considered essential aspects of a believer's duty.
